entries.description: A daily job checks the reverse DNS of the system IPs against the name exim greets with and raises a banner for the admin when one does not match. One line added to the hestia crontab, the rest stays as it is, and the check runs once right away

CrowdSec honours the firewall whitelist and a domain's CrowdSec switch: a whitelisted address and the log of a domain switched off are no longer counted, so no ban arises from them. A domain without a choice yet, i.e. one created before the default, gets the default and is switched on

Sieve reject is switched off on dovecot 2.3: it mailed its refusal to the envelope sender, which spam forges. Neither webmail offers the action any more; a script that still uses it no longer compiles, and its mail goes to the inbox. Skipped where the line was changed by hand
Sieve reject is switched off on dovecot 2.4, the same as on 2.3. Skipped where the commented sieve_extensions block was changed by hand

PostgreSQL takes a password over its local socket for every role but postgres, which keeps peer, so a customer's container can log in to a database from the panel. Before, the socket allowed peer only, which a Hestia role never passes. A role whose password is still an md5 hash logs in over neither the socket nor TCP and needs a new password. Skipped where the line was changed by hand
